What's new

Version 135 · Halden Off-Road Park, Grand Cherokee L, Grand Wagoneer L, 2022 Palisade

Halden Off-Road Park

  • A new off-road park in the hills west of County Rd 12 (pick Off-road park in the start menu, or turn in at the trailhead lot just south of the proving ground). A dirt trail loops through it with a board at every obstacle, rated like a real park: green circle, blue square, black diamond.
  • Boulder Alley (black diamond): a 120 m rock garden. Every rock is its own shape: chipped faces, flat tops, cracks, some leaning, in granite gray, sandstone tan and dark basalt, with big boulders walling the trail in. The rocks you see are exactly what your tyres climb.
  • The Steps (blue square): three rock ledges, 30 to 45 cm high.
  • The Bog (blue square): a sunken mud pit about 60 cm deep with ruts and muddy water at the bottom. Keep your momentum.
  • Log Crossing (green circle): three logs across the trail.
  • Off-Camber (blue square): a section where the trail tilts about 15°.
  • Widowmaker (black diamond): an 8 m hill with a 30% climb.
  • The trees in the park are solid, so stay on the trail. Crawl Control, Trail Control, Selec-Speed, lockers and the terrain modes all work here.

New Jeeps and an older Palisade

  • 2026 Jeep Grand Cherokee L (3 rows): Laredo 4x2 (3.6 V6, 293 hp), Limited and Limited Reserve 4x4 (2.0 Hurricane, 324 hp), Summit 4x4 with Quadra-Lift air suspension.
  • 2026 Jeep Grand Wagoneer L (long-wheelbase): 4x4, Limited and Summit Reserve, 3.0 Hurricane twin-turbo I6 (420 hp), Quadra-Lift air suspension.
  • 2022 Hyundai Palisade (the first generation): SE, SEL, Limited and Calligraphy, 3.8 V6 (291 hp). Limited and Calligraphy have HTRAC AWD and Highway Driving Assist.
  • New, more detailed bodies for the Jeep Compass, Cherokee, Grand Cherokee, Grand Wagoneer, Wagoneer S and Recon.

Version 134 · New left-side dock

Left-side buttons

  • The key, phone and Bluetooth buttons are now one glass dock, and each shows its state underneath: Locked (green) or Unlocked (amber) with a padlock that opens and closes, Linked (blue) when your phone is connected, and a red badge on the phone for unread messages.
  • The Screen button moved into the dock. It only shows in the driver's seat view and switches to Road while you're looking at the screen.
  • The little arrow under the dock shrinks it to icons only; it remembers your choice.

Version 133 · Valet parking job

Halden Valet

  • New gig in the phone's Gig Jobs app: 🔑 Valet. Start a shift, park your own car near the Cass Ave garage and walk to the valet stand on the sidewalk.
  • Guests pull up at the curb in nice cars (BMW, Escalade, Lucid, Rivian, Mercedes and more). Walk up, take the keys, drive it into the garage and park it in any free stall on any level, nose in between the lines. Shift to P and get out.
  • When a guest is ready to leave you get their ticket number and level. Tap Run there to jog to the car, then bring it down to the stand. The guest drives away in it.
  • Pay is $7 a car plus a tip for speed: up to $14 for parking and $25 for a quick return. Any new dent or scratch costs you the tip and comes out of your pay. Keep it under 15 mph in the garage.
  • The garage gates open for you on the job, and a yellow marker shows the car or the stand. Your own car waits where you left it, with its fuel and damage just as they were.

Version 132 · Escalade lower screen, tire air machines, Hwy 7 toll plaza

Cadillac Escalade

  • The main touchscreen now lives in the lower screen under the 55-inch display, where the real 2026 Escalade has it. The big curved screen shows the gauges, the map and the clock, weather and media across the dash.

Tire air at gas stations

  • Every gas station now has a red air machine near the pumps. Park close, walk up and tap Air for your tires · $2.00: all four tires go back to 35 psi. A slow leak keeps leaking until it's patched (phone › car app, or Tread Center).

Toll plaza on Hwy 7

  • A toll plaza with booths in every lane, a canopy and lane lights, in both directions. The toll is $2.50 ($5.00 with a trailer).
  • Right lane, CASH: stop at the booth, pay, and the gate arm lifts. Drive through it and you break the gate and get a $50 violation by mail.
  • Other lanes, E-ZPass: with a tag ($10 in Settings › Assists › Your car) the toll comes off as you pass. Without one, a toll-by-plate bill with a $5 fee arrives in the mail.
  • Traffic slows down for the plaza, stays in its lane, and cars in the cash lane stop at the booth.

Version 131 · Engine heat, hot brakes, fuel grades, dashcam replays, off-road tools and more

Where to find them

  • Settings › Assists, under the safety systems: Off-road, your car's air suspension, More car features and a Your car summary (outside temperature, engine temperature, fuel, alignment, alarm, dashcam, insurance, updates and recalls).

Driving

  • Outside temperature now follows the season and time of day (cold January mornings, hot July afternoons, the odd heat wave), and the screens show it.
  • Engine heat: slow traffic on a hot day, towing something heavy or a cracked radiator push the temperature up. Around 112 °C the A/C switches itself off; above 117 °C you lose power until it cools. The gauge on the cluster moves.
  • Hot brakes: ride the brakes down a long hill and you get a hot-brake smell warning, then brake fade (a soft pedal) and smoke from the wheels.
  • Alignment: a hard pothole hit can knock it out. The car pulls to one side and wears its tires faster until Tread Center fixes it ($129).
  • Rev-matching on manual downshifts for the cars that have it (Civic Type R, Integra Type S). In other cars, blip the throttle with the clutch in or the car lurches.

Fuel

  • Pick a grade at the pump: Regular 87, Midgrade 89 or Premium 93. Cars that need premium lose about 6% power on regular; turbo engines that only recommend it lose a little.
  • Fuel door and charge port on the correct side for the cars we know. The arrow next to the fuel (or battery) icon shows which side; park with the pump on that side or the hose won't reach.

Security and cameras

  • While you're away from your parked car, someone may try the door. Locked cars set off the alarm and your brand's app sends an alert (myChevrolet, FordPass, Toyota app, and so on). Unlocked cars get robbed.
  • Tesla Sentry Mode and Rivian Gear Guard flash the lights and save a clip. Dog Mode (Tesla) and Pet Comfort (Rivian) show the "My owner will be back soon" screen.
  • Locked doors now stop the person who walks up to your car at a red light.
  • Dashcam replays: on cars with a dashcam (Tesla, Rivian, newer Hyundai/Kia/Genesis Built-in Cam, BMW Drive Recorder, Mercedes, or the dealer add-on), crashes and near misses save the last 30 seconds. Watch them back with slow-mo; F8 replays the last 30 seconds any time.

Owning the car

  • Insurance: tickets raise your premium for 3 years. At the body shop you can file a claim: insurance pays, you pay the $500 deductible, and the premium goes up for 3 years.
  • Software updates over the air on the brands that really send them (Tesla, Rivian, Lucid, Ford Power-Up, GM, BMW, Mercedes, Hyundai/Kia/Genesis, Volvo, VW, Audi, Toyota and Lexus). BlueCruise and Super Cruise cars without lane changes get them in an update. You install from Settings while parked.
  • Recalls: now and then a recall notice arrives for your model, and you may notice the problem (a rear camera that blacks out, an engine that runs hot or stalls, charging capped at 80%). Dealer service at Tread Center fixes it for free, along with an inspection, any update, alignment and oil. It's free in the first 2 years on Toyota and Lexus and 3 years on BMW.

Off-road and suspension

  • Low-speed off-road cruise under each brand's name: Toyota CRAWL Control, Lexus Crawl Control, Ford Trail Control, Jeep Selec-Speed Control.
  • Ford Trail 1-Pedal Drive and GM Terrain mode: lift off and the truck brakes for you. Ford Trail Turn Assist turns about 20% tighter.
  • Lockers on pavement now scrub and fight the turn, like real ones.
  • Air suspension heights on Ram (Active-Level), Jeep (Quadra-Lift), Chevy/GMC/Cadillac (Air Ride) and Rivian: Entry/Exit (lowers when you park and get out), Aero (drops above 55 mph), Normal and off-road heights with their real speed limits.
  • Night vision on cars that have it (Cadillac and GMC Night Vision, Jeep Night Vision Camera, Audi Night vision assist): a thermal picture at night with people and animals boxed in yellow.

Version 130 · Rivian R1T, R1S and R2

New brand: Rivian (9 trims)

  • 2027 Rivian R1T pickup: Premium (dual motor, 533 hp, about 329 mi), Performance (tri motor, 850 hp, 0-60 in 2.9 s) and Quad (a motor at each wheel, 1,025 hp). From $79,990.
  • 2027 Rivian R1S three-row SUV: the same Premium, Performance and Quad trims. From $83,990.
  • 2027 Rivian R2: Standard (rear-drive, 350 hp, about 345 mi), Premium (dual motor, 450 hp) and Performance Launch Edition (656 hp, 0-60 in 3.6 s, with Universal Hands-Free driving). From $48,490.
  • Real Rivian drive modes: All-Purpose, Conserve, Sport, Snow, All-Terrain and Towing, plus Soft Sand and Rally on the Performance and Quad trims and Rock Crawl on the Quad.
  • R1 has air suspension that raises and lowers (7.9 to 14.4 in. of ground clearance) with hydraulic roll control. R2 has coil springs, with semi-active dampers on the Performance.
  • Highway Assist on every Rivian, the Rivian screen colors, a dark glass roof, the light bar and stadium headlights. The Rivians also show up in traffic.

Version 129 · 19 new safety systems, each on the cars that really have them

Where to find them

  • Settings › Assists › More safety systems lists every one your car has, under the maker's own name (BlueCruise, OnStar, MyKey, Safe Exit Assist and so on). Each has an on/off switch. Cars that never had a system don't get it.

Towing

  • Trailer sway control on tow-rated cars from 2010 on: when a heavy trailer starts to sway, the car brakes and calms it down.
  • Pro Trailer Backup Assist (F-150 2021+, Super Duty, Ranger 2024+, Expedition 2022+) and Trailer Reverse Steering Control (Ram 1500/2500/3500): in reverse, steer the way you want the trailer to go and the truck steers itself. The rear camera shows the trailer angle.
  • Trailer Reverse Guidance (Silverado, Sierra) and Trailer Backup Guide (Tundra, Sequoia): trailer path lines in the rear camera.
  • Transparent Trailer View (Silverado, Sierra): the rear camera sees through your trailer.
  • Drop the trailer (Settings › Spawn) and hook it up again by backing up to it. Hitch guidance shows a line to the coupler and the distance: Hitch Guidance with Hitch View (GM trucks and big SUVs), Trailer Hitch Zoom (Ram), Hitch view (Tundra, Sequoia). F-150 and Super Duty get Pro Trailer Hitch Assist, which backs up to the trailer by itself.
  • Blind spot with trailer coverage (Ford BLIS, GM Trailer Side Blind Zone Alert, Ram, Grand Cherokee, Wagoneer, Tundra, Sequoia): the blind-spot lights cover the length of your trailer.

Watching the driver

  • Drowsiness alerts (Ford Driver Alert, Honda Driver Attention Monitor, Mercedes ATTENTION ASSIST, Volvo Driver Alert Control and others): a coffee-break reminder after about 25 minutes of driving, and a warning if you weave in your lane.
  • Hands-free systems watch your eyes (Super Cruise, BlueCruise, Autopilot, ProPILOT 2.1): have your phone open too long while it's driving and it warns you, then turns itself off.
  • Emergency stop (Super Cruise, BlueCruise, Toyota and Lexus 2023+, Mercedes, BMW, VW, Audi, Volvo, Tesla, Lucid): if lane centering is on and you don't touch anything for a long time, it beeps, then slows to a stop in your lane with the hazards on and calls for help.

Around you

  • Safe Exit Assist: when you get out with a car or bike coming up beside you, it warns you. Hyundai, Kia, Genesis and Lexus keep the door locked (press again to open anyway).
  • Front cross-traffic alert (Mazda CX-5/50/70/90, Lexus, Audi, BMW, Lucid, Sequoia, Tundra, Grand Highlander, Crown): beeps when you pull out slowly with traffic coming from the side.
  • Turning braking (Toyota Intersection Support, Hyundai/Kia Junction Turning, Ford Intersection Assist, VW/Audi Turn Assist and others): brakes if you turn left in front of an oncoming car.
  • Wrong-way alert (Ford, Lincoln, Mercedes, BMW, VW, Audi, Volvo, Tesla, Lucid): drive the wrong way up a ramp and it warns you.
  • Railroad alerts: with your phone connected (CarPlay / Android Auto), Waze warns you about a train at a crossing ahead and if you stop on the tracks. Teslas show it on their own.

After a crash

  • Automatic crash notification (OnStar, SYNC 911 Assist, Toyota Safety Connect, Uconnect SOS, Blue Link and more): after a hard crash an advisor calls. Say you're okay, or tap Send help (or don't answer for 15 seconds) and an ambulance and tow truck drive to you.
  • Post-collision braking (VW, Audi, Mercedes, BMW, Volvo, Ford 2020+, Hyundai/Kia/Genesis 2020+): the car brakes after an impact so you don't roll into a second crash.
  • Emergency vehicles drive in with lights and siren, and traffic slows and moves over for them. Jeep, Ram, Dodge and Chrysler 2018+ warn you ahead of time (Uconnect Safety Cloud), and so do Teslas.

Tires, wipers, other drivers

  • Tire pressure monitoring on every car: hard pothole hits can start a slow leak and snow drops the pressure. You get a TPMS warning, and the phone's car app shows each tire's psi with a $35 patch-and-fill. The 2007 cars only have the warning light.
  • Wipers you can see on the windshield. Press ; to go Off, Intermittent, Low, High. Cars with rain-sensing wipers (luxury brands and upper trims) start them by themselves when it rains.
  • Teen Driver (GM, 85 mph limit), MyKey (Ford, 65–80 mph), Speed Limit Mode (Tesla), Care Key (Volvo), Valet Mode (Dodge, Hyundai, Kia) and speed alerts (Toyota Guest Driver, Honda, Subaru, VW, Nissan), each with a driving report.

Version 128 · New freight train, real trailers, traffic sees your trailer

Freight train

  • The old box train is gone. A real freight train now runs the line: a diesel locomotive (cab, roof fans, handrails, headlights) pulling boxcars and coal hoppers, 7 cars and about 90 m long.
  • Each car rides on its two bogies, so the train bends properly through the curves and up and down the ramps. It sits on the rails on the viaduct and at street level.
  • It works with the crossings: the gates stay down until the last car has passed, the headlights flash with the horn, and you can't drive through any of the cars.

Trailers

  • All three trailers are new detailed models:
    • Utility trailer: wood deck, rails and a loading gate.
    • Travel camper: tandem axles, entry door, windows, awning and roof AC.
    • Boat on a trailer: a bowrider with an outboard motor, on bunks with a winch.
  • Each one hitches at its real ball coupler and turns around its real axles. Its brake lights and tail lights work with yours.
  • Traffic sees your trailer: AI cars now stop behind it or change lanes to pass it instead of driving through it.

Version 127 · GM My Mode you can set up, Escalade mirror fix

My Mode (Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC)

  • My Mode is now customizable like the real car's Drive Mode app: Settings › Car › My Mode settings. Pick My Mode in the drive modes to drive with them. Your settings are saved for each car.
  • Cadillac LYRIQ, OPTIQ, VISTIQ, CELESTIQ: Motor Sound (Tour, Sport, Stealth, and V on V-Series), Acceleration Feel (Relaxed, Tour, Sport), Brake Feel, Steering, Suspension (cars with adaptive dampers) and Competitive Mode (V-Series).
  • Chevrolet and GMC EVs (Blazer EV, Equinox EV, Silverado EV, Sierra EV, HUMMER EV): Acceleration Feel (Relaxed, Normal, Sport), Brake Feel, Steering, and Motor Sound (Normal, Sport, Off).
  • Escalade: Engine Sound, Steering and Brake Feel (Tour or Sport).
  • You can feel each setting: Relaxed softens the pedal and Sport sharpens it, Sport steering responds quicker, and Sport brake feel stops harder for the same pedal. Sport suspension firms the dampers, Competitive Mode loosens traction control, and motor or engine sound goes from silent to loud.

Fixes

  • Escalade rear-view mirror now hangs from the top of the windshield instead of floating in the middle of the glass. The same fix applies to every car that gets the windshield-mounted mirror.

Version 126 · Buy out your lease

  • Lease buyout: you can now buy a leased car outright instead of giving it back. The price is what's left on the lease, plus the car's residual value (58% of what it cost new), plus a $350 purchase-option fee.
  • Do it from My Garage (the car button, top right) with Buy out the lease, or from the Northline Bank app under Pay.
  • Once it's bought out, the lease payments stop and the car is yours to keep, sell or trade in.

Version 125 · Crossing signals off the road, rails you can see

  • Crossing signals moved off the road. Each mast now stands just past the edge of the road (on wide and divided roads too), not in a lane or the bike lane. The gate arm is sized to reach across the lanes it closes.
  • Warning signs off the bike lane. The round yellow railroad warning signs stand beside the road, clear of the bike lanes.
  • Road markings in the right place. The X, the R R and the stop line sit across the approach lanes.
  • Traffic stops in every lane at the crossing, including on divided roads.
  • Rails across the road. The steel rails now show through the concrete crossing panels, with the dark gaps beside them, so you can see the track run across the road.

Version 124 · Real railroad crossings

  • Crossing signals like the real thing: a white crossbuck with a black edge, two red lamps with black backboards and visors flashing back and forth, a bell on top, and a footing at the base of the mast.
  • Real gates: the lights start flashing first, the gates start down 4 seconds later and take about 10 seconds to lower. The arm has red and white stripes, three red lamps (the tip one stays on) and a counterweight. The train reaches the road about 25 seconds after the lights come on, and the gates go back up once it has passed.
  • The bell rings until the gates are down, like most real crossings.
  • The train sounds its horn for every crossing: long, long, short, long. Its ditch lights flash while it does.
  • Warning signs and road markings: a round yellow railroad warning sign 110 m before each crossing, a big painted X and R R on the lane, and a stop line before the gate.
  • Track you can see: wooden ties under the rails where the track runs at ground level, and concrete panels where it crosses the road.

Version 123 · Photos, texts, radio ads, a better Maps app, low-end mode, first-drive tutorial

Phone

  • 📷 Photos app: take a picture of the view with the HUD hidden (or press F9 on PC). Up to 24 are kept on your device, and you can open, save or delete each one.
  • 💬 Texts: Marcus (your friend), Mom, Dana from Halden Freight, Tread Center, the bank and the radio station text you now and then. Some react to what you do: a big crash, stopping a robbery, a new exhaust or wrap, your gig earnings, snow on the way.
  • 🗺 Maps: one tap to the nearest gas station, Tread Center or your current job stop, plus every place on the map. Road work, closed roads and a getaway car now show up on the map too.
  • 📻 Radio ads: every few minutes the music dips for a local ad (Tread Center, Bean & Brew, Strata Motors, Halden Freight…) and the station ID, like real radio.

Settings

  • 📱 Low-end phone mode (Settings › Graphics): one tap for Lowest graphics, 30 fps, simple mirrors, the solid HUD and fewer random events. Tap again to put everything back.

New players

  • First-drive tutorial: a short guide on your first drive: seatbelt, starting the car, Drive, getting up to speed, signalling and the phone. It moves on as you do each step, and you can skip it. To see it again: Settings › Controls › Show the tutorial.

Version 122 · Taxi, tow truck and freight jobs, trade-ins

New jobs in the Gig Jobs app

  • 🚕 Halden Taxi: a TAXI sign goes on your roof. Fares are metered: $3.50 to start plus $2.80 for every mile you actually drive with the passenger. Smooth rides earn a 12–22% tip.
  • 🛻 Tow Truck: find a broken-down car with its hazards on, stop next to it to hook it up, then tow it to the repair shop. It follows on the hook behind you. About $95 plus $3.20 a mile, and 20% less if you hit something on the way. Needs a truck or big SUV.
  • 🚚 Halden Freight: load about 900 lb of pallets at the depot and drop them at 2 or 3 businesses. You feel the weight until it's all delivered. Around $95–150 a run. Needs a van, minivan, truck or big SUV.

Selling and trading in

  • Trade-ins: when you buy, finance or lease a car, pick one of yours under Trade in a car. Its value comes off the price, any loan on it is paid off, and it leaves your garage when you sign.
  • Condition counts: what you get when you sell or trade in now drops for damage, bald tyres, worn brakes and overdue oil changes. Fix it up first and you get more.

Version 121 · Tuning shop, body shop, manual gearbox, trailers, battery health

Tuning (at Tread Center)

  • Power: Stage 1 ECU tune (+8%), Stage 2 (+13%, or +22% on turbo engines), or a Power unlock for EVs (+12%). A stage 2 Camry goes 0-60 about a second quicker.
  • Lowering springs: 35 mm lower, less body roll and a little more grip.
  • Sport exhaust: much louder and deeper, inside and out.
  • Window tint: 35% or 5% limo. You only see it from outside, so your view isn't darker.
  • Wraps: matte black, satin battleship gray, Nardo gray, matte army green, gloss race red, satin midnight blue, candy purple and silver chrome.
  • Wheels: gloss black, bronze, chrome or gunmetal.
  • Everything stays with the car you own, and you can put any of it back to stock.

Damage and the body shop

  • A hard hit leaves the bumper hanging off at the front or back. A bad front hit cracks the windshield (you see the crack from the driver's seat) and a smashed front end smokes.
  • The body shop prices repairs part by part: front end, rear end, each side, windshield, lights and dents. Fix just what you want, or everything at once.

Manual gearbox

  • Any gas car with a regular automatic can now be driven with a clutch: Settings › Controls › Manual gearbox with clutch. Ctrl is the clutch, Q shifts up, E shifts down (below 1st is neutral, then reverse when you're stopped).
  • On phones there are ▲ ▼ and CLUTCH buttons on the right.
  • Shift without the clutch and it grinds. Stop in gear without the clutch and it stalls. Press the clutch to restart.

Trailers

  • Trucks and big SUVs can hitch a utility trailer, a travel camper or a boat (Settings › Spawn).
  • The trailer follows the hitch like a real one: it cuts corners, and in reverse it swings the other way and can jackknife.
  • Its weight makes the car slower to speed up and to stop, and a heavy one sways above 65 mph.

Car condition

  • EV battery health: it fades about 8% per 100,000 miles and a little each year (never below 70%), and your range drops with it. Tread Center shows the health and can fit a new pack.

Version 120 · Puddles and black ice, rush hour, real crashes, road work, level crossings, robberies

Weather

  • Puddles. When it rains, puddles fill up in the lanes. Hit one above about 40 mph and that side of the car aquaplanes and loses almost all grip. Ease off, don't slam the brakes.
  • Black ice. In snow, the puddles freeze into ice patches. Bridges and overpasses freeze first, so expect very little grip on them.
  • Thicker fog. You can see much less in fog now.

Traffic

  • Traffic follows the clock. It's about 50% busier at rush hour (6:30–9:30 am and 3:30–6:30 pm) and nearly empty from midnight to 5 am.
  • Late-night drivers. After 10 pm more drivers are aggressive, and a few are drunk: they weave in their lane and their speed keeps changing.

Crashes and road work

  • Traffic cars crash into each other. Now and then a car ahead brakes hard and the one behind isn't paying attention. They stop where they hit with hazards on and cones behind. An ambulance and a tow truck arrive with flashing lights, then the tow truck clears it about 2 minutes later.
  • Road work that moves every day. Each in-game day a few busy roads get a lane coned off for about 150 m, with a road-work sign and a work truck.
  • Road closed, detour. Each day one side street is closed at both ends with barriers. Traffic and your navigation route around it, and you get a warning if you head for it.

Level crossings

  • The train line now comes down to street level in four places and crosses roads at 5 level crossings. The gates come down, the lights flash, the bell rings and traffic waits. Don't race the train.

Crime

  • Gas station robberies. Near a gas station, you might see a robber run out and jump into a getaway car that tears off. Ram it to stop it ($750 reward), or stay within 40 m of it for 30 seconds until it's caught ($400).
  • Door grabs at night. Sit stopped in town late at night and someone may walk up to your door. Drive off within 3 seconds or they'll grab your wallet ($150–500).
  • Both follow Settings › World › Random events, so set that to Off if you don't want them.

Version 119 · The police remember you

Police

  • Getting away isn't the end. When you lose the cops, they remember your car (model and colour) and how wanted you were. Grey stars at the top show it, with a countdown: "They're looking for this car".
  • Spotted again? If any police car sees that car within 60 m during the countdown, the chase starts right back up at the stars you got away with.
  • How long they remember: 2 minutes plus 1 minute per star (5 minutes after a 3-star escape). It's remembered even if you reload the game.
  • Lie low: wait it out, or swap to a different car or a new paint colour and they won't recognise you. Paying a ticket or getting busted clears it too.

Version 118 · New rear-view mirrors, solid HUD option, police off switch, newer cars in traffic

Mirrors and screens

  • One rear-view mirror for every car. Each model's old built-in mirror is gone and the new mirror replaces it in the same spot: glass that shows the road behind, a dark housing and a stem up to the windshield. Cars that had no mirror get one hanging from the top of the windshield.
  • 2019 RAV4 screen fits. The Entune screen now sits flush inside the dash bezel instead of sticking out past it at the bottom right.

HUD

  • Solid HUD. Don't like the see-through glass? Settings › Car › HUD look › Solid gives you opaque dark panels with no blur. It's easier to read and lighter on older phones. Your choice is remembered.

Police

  • Turn the police off completely. Settings › Spawn › Turn off police (or Settings › Controls › Police). No patrol cars anywhere in traffic, no tickets and no chases. Remembered on this device.

Traffic

  • Newer cars on the road. A random set of the newer cars (Lucid, Mazda, VW, BMW, Hyundai, Cadillac, Tesla and more) now loads in the background and joins the AI traffic. About 3 in 10 traffic cars are now one of them, and the set changes every time you play.

Version 117 · Cops pull in behind you, drive like traffic, and you can spawn them

Police

  • Getting pulled over. When you slow down and stop for a 1-star stop, the cruiser pulls in about 8 m behind you, lined up with your car, lights flashing. Once it's parked the officer writes the ticket, then the cruiser pulls back out into traffic.
  • Cruisers move like traffic cars. Same suspension as the AI cars: the nose dips under braking, it squats when it pulls away and leans in corners. It also tilts with hills and ramps. Acceleration and braking are now realistic instead of instant.
  • Cops don't drive through other cars. They slow down behind traffic and swing out to pass it.
  • Spawn the police yourself. Settings › Spawn has two new buttons. Spawn a police car puts a patrol car in traffic just behind you. Start a police chase gets you 2 stars straight away.

Other

  • The car button at the top right now opens My Garage with all the cars you own, so you can switch to one.

Version 116 · Outrun the cops, $10,000 Busted, mirrors that sit on the car

Police

  • You can outrun them now. Cruisers top out around 98 mph and slow down for bends like real traffic. Get more than 200 m away and stay out of sight for 10 seconds to drop a star. At 2 stars that means you've lost them.
  • Busted. Stop during a chase with a cop nearby for 3 seconds and a big BUSTED screen comes up. You pay a $10,000 fine and your car is towed.
  • Cops stay on the road. They follow the roads you took, keep to their lane and slow for corners instead of cutting across the grass. When the chase ends they rejoin traffic and drive normally (signals, lanes, junctions) instead of driving off in a straight line.
  • Cops don't crash into each other. Cruisers keep a gap to the one in front, spread across the lanes behind you and never overlap.
  • Cops no longer teleport back to you when you get far ahead.

Mirrors

  • Door mirror glass sits on the mirror. It now fills the back of each car's own mirror housing instead of floating off to the side. This was worst on the Escalade, Ram, Silverado, Tacoma and other trucks.
  • The rear-view mirror is on the car's own mirror by the windshield, not floating out past the glass. Cars without one in the model get a mirror with a stem hanging from the top of the windshield.
  • The blind spot lights are now in the corner of the mirror glass, like real cars, and stay dark when off.

Version 115 · Police pursuits, Lucid Air and Gravity, new Escalade

Police

  • Cops pull you over now. Speed past a police car, run someone over or hit a cruiser and you get a wanted star. Its lights come on and it follows you.
  • Pull over and stop with the cruiser behind you and after a few seconds you just get a ticket ($150 plus $12 for every mph over).
  • Keep driving and it turns into a chase, with stars at the top of the screen like GTA. More stars the longer you run, up to 5.
  • They do whatever it takes: 3 stars and they ram you, 4 stars and they lay spike strips ahead (a flat tyre slows you right down), 5 stars and two cruisers block the road.
  • Busted: if they box you in and you stop for 3 seconds, you pay a fine for every star and your car is towed.
  • Lose them: get more than 300 m away and stay out of sight for 25 seconds to drop a star. Sirens and flashing red and blue lights the whole way.
  • Don't want cops? Turn them off in Settings › Controls › Police.

New cars (6 trims)

  • 2026 Lucid Air: Pure (430 hp, RWD, 420 mi), Touring (620 hp), Grand Touring (819 hp, 512 mi) and Sapphire (1,234 hp, 0-60 in 1.89 s). Smooth, Swift and Sprint modes, plus Sapphire mode on the Sapphire.
  • 2026 Lucid Gravity: Touring (450 hp) and Grand Touring (828 hp, 450 mi). 7 seats, air suspension and a Terrain mode.
  • Both have the Lucid curved glass cluster and the center Pilot Panel screen.

Cadillac Escalade

  • New 2026 Escalade body and interior. The 55-inch curved screen now sits where it really does, with the gauges on the left and the center screen on the right.

Version 114 · Real screens and gauges for VW, RAV4, Honda, Audi, Jeep, Escalade, Dodge, Ram and Chrysler

Infotainment screens

  • Volkswagen: the big floating screen. A map tile, the audio card with green borders, IDA and Sound tiles, and the bottom climate bar with temperatures, CLIMA, AUTO, A/C and shortcuts.
  • 2019 RAV4: the 8-inch Entune 3.0 with the real hard buttons (HOME, MENU, AUDIO, MAP, SEEK, TRACK, PHONE, APPS) and both knobs. Home is the split screen with audio, CarPlay / Android Auto and the map. The Radio page has the list on the left and six presets.
  • Honda: the 9-inch Display Audio home with colored tiles: All Apps, Navigation, Phone, FM, Bluetooth Audio, Smartphone Connection, Vehicle, and Power flow on hybrids.
  • Audi (newer models): MMI touch response. Tiles on the upper screen and a climate panel below.
  • Jeep: the wide Uconnect 5 with the app grid and a clock card. Dodge: the red Uconnect SRT screen with Race Options as home (shift light per gear, launch control) and the Home / Media / Comfort / Nav / Phone / Vehicle / Apps bar. Ram: the 12-inch Uconnect with the map on top and the FM and Phone cards below.
  • Escalade: the 55-inch OLED home with trip info and the app grid. LYRIQ, OPTIQ, VISTIQ: the 33-inch home with two rows of apps, the small dock, and the temperature and time.

Gauge clusters

  • Volkswagen Digital Cockpit with blue-ringed tachometer and speedometer, side bars, and speed limit and clock along the top.
  • 2019 RAV4 hybrid ECO / POWER / CHARGE meter (a tachometer on gas models), with the speedometer and what's playing.
  • Honda power meter with EV / READY on hybrids, or a tachometer, plus the speedometer, the car in its lane and the fuel bar.
  • 2019 Audi Q5 big blue-faced dials. Escalade line-style tachometer with the navigation card. Chrysler glowing blue rings with the Vehicle Info screen. Ram blue-arc dials with the big center speed, DEF and fuel.
  • Base trims that really have analog dials keep them.

Version 113 · Four classic cars, touchpad and phone fixes

New cars (19 trims)

  • 2010 Acura MDX: Base, Technology, Entertainment and Advance. 300 hp V6 with SH-AWD. The Advance has adaptive cruise, Collision Mitigation Braking and Active Dampers.
  • 2017 Ford Fusion: S, SE, Titanium, Sport (325 hp twin-turbo V6, AWD), Platinum, Hybrid and Energi plug-in.
  • 2007 Ford Mustang: V6, V6 Premium, GT, GT Premium and the 500 hp Shelby GT500.
  • 2007 Kia Sportage: LX, LX V6 4WD and EX V6.
  • These older cars only have the driver aids they really had, with analog gauges and their original colors and prices.

Fixes

  • Touchpads work again. Click and drag anywhere to look around. A plain click on the car's screen or a dash button still presses it. Right-drag still works with a mouse.
  • Phone and key buttons on PC. The phone, key fob and Bluetooth buttons now show on the left side on PC and laptops too, so you can click to open your phone in the car.
  • Cadillac interiors. The floating posts in front of the driver in the LYRIQ, OPTIQ, VISTIQ and CELESTIQ are gone. The Hyundai, BMW and Mercedes-Benz interiors got the same cleanup.

Version 112 · Sit higher, adjust the steering wheel

  • Sit higher. The seat now goes up to Higher (+12 cm) and Highest (+18 cm), so you can see over tall dashboards and steering wheels. Settings › Controls › Seat.
  • Steering wheel adjustment. Tilt it down (Lowest, Low, Middle, High) to see the gauges and the road over it, and set the reach closer or farther away. Your hands follow the wheel. Settings › Controls › Steering wheel.

Version 111 · Smaller HUD, hide the HUD, Get in on mobile

  • Smaller HUD. Everything on screen is about 15% smaller on PC and mobile, so you see more road. Pick Small, Medium, Large or Extra large in Settings › Car › HUD size.
  • Hide the HUD. Tap the new eye button at the top left (or press F2 on PC) to clear the screen for screenshots and cruising. On mobile the pedals and steering arrows stay so you can keep driving. Tap the eye again to bring everything back.
  • Get back in the car on mobile. When you walk up to your car's door, a Get in button appears at the bottom. It also shows the other on-foot actions, like Fill up, Plug in and Unplug. On PC, O or U does the same.

Version 110 · A whole new look

New HUD on PC and mobile

  • Every on-screen control is now frosted dark glass with thin borders, so you can see the road through it.
  • Anything switched on (signals, lights, Drive, EV mode, the selected gear) glows mint. Hazards and the parking brake glow red, and Accessory mode glows amber.
  • Speed is bigger and easier to read, in a cleaner cluster with thin glowing gas and brake bars. The fuel or charge bar glows too.
  • The brake and Drive pedals have new glass faces with lit labels. The settings menu, Where-to-go pop-up, messages and navigation card match the new style.

Phone

  • The Stocks and Gig Jobs apps now show on the phone's home screen. They were missing from it before.

Cornering lights are back

  • 184 trims that really have cornering or steering-responsive headlights get them back, for example Mazda AFS, VW dynamic cornering lights, BMW adaptive LEDs, Mercedes Active Light System, Lexus, Lincoln, Volvo Active Bending Lights and Subaru Steering Responsive Headlights. Cars without them stay without.

Version 109 · Real-world money, stocks, cleaner settings

Money works like real life

  • Out-the-door prices. Buying a car now adds what a real dealer charges: destination fee, 6% sales tax, a $260 doc fee and $183 for title and plates. The full breakdown shows before you pay. A $28,875 Camry LE comes to $32,529.
  • Car insurance. Every car you own costs a weekly premium, based on the car's price and your credit score. A Camry is about $34 a week. It comes out of checking, or goes on your credit card if checking is short.
  • No more money for just driving. You earned about $16 a mile before. Driving now gives XP only. Earn money with the Gig Jobs app or the stock market. Level-ups pay $100.
  • New games start with $2,500 in checking. Package delivery pays about $6.50 a stop plus mileage, closer to real delivery work.

Stocks (new phone app)

  • Invest in 12 companies plus an index fund. Prices move while you play, each with its own trend and risk. Some pay a weekly dividend.
  • Buy and sell 1, 10, 100 or as many shares as you can afford, from checking. You'll see your portfolio's value, today's change and a price chart.

Settings

  • The long list of every car is gone from Settings › Car. Change cars with Change car (the car builder) instead.

Version 108 · Mouse fixes, FCW only where it's fitted

  • One click is enough. Buttons in the phone, menus and panels sometimes needed a double click because the panel refreshed between press and release. A single left click now always works.
  • Left click selects, right click looks around. Left-click the car's screen, dash buttons and menus. Hold the right button and drag to look around (or turn the outside camera).
  • No more right-click menu. Right-clicking the game no longer pops up "Copy image" / "Save image as".
  • Forward collision warning and auto braking only on cars that have them. The 2011 SX4 has neither, so it no longer shows the BRAKE! warning or brakes for you. Every other car in the game has them as standard.

Version 107 · Gig Jobs app, build options and suspension for the new cars

Gig Jobs (new phone app)

  • Earn money driving. Pick Packages (a route of 3 to 5 drop-offs from the delivery station), Food (pick up at a restaurant, deliver before the deadline) or Rides (pick up a rider and drive them to their destination), then tap Go online.
  • Offers pop up every 10 to 25 seconds with the pay, distance and time. Accept one and the route goes into navigation. Stop within 20 m of each stop to pick up or drop off.
  • Pay goes straight into your Northline checking account. Late food loses the tip and part of the pay. Riders rate your driving: crashes and hard braking cost stars and tips.

Build & Price for the new cars

  • Every Hyundai, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Cadillac, Mazda, Volkswagen, 2026 RAV4, Cybertruck and 2020 Model S / X now has its real packages, options, wheels, interiors, paint colors and accessories in the car builder, with each trim's standard equipment.

Suspension

  • All 188 cars that were still on the generic setup now have their real suspension. Examples: torsion-beam rear on the Mazda3 and Jetta, air suspension with active anti-roll on the BMW X5 / X7 M60i, AIRMATIC and E-ACTIVE BODY CONTROL on the Mercedes GLE / GLS, Magnetic Ride on the Cadillac V models, a solid rear axle on the G-Class, off-road tuning on the XRT, Woodland, Meridian and Peak trims, and the Cybertruck's adjustable air suspension. Ride height, body roll and the Suspension name in settings follow each car.

Version 106 · Mazda and Volkswagen, new Teslas, RAV4 2026, city vehicles

New cars (78 trims)

  • Mazda: Mazda3 Hatchback, CX-30, the all-new 2026 CX-5, CX-50 (gas, turbo and hybrid), CX-70 and CX-90 (inline-6 turbo and plug-in hybrid). Every trim from Select Sport to Turbo S Premium Plus.
  • Volkswagen: Jetta (including GLI Autobahn), Taos, Tiguan, Atlas, Atlas Cross Sport, ID.4 and ID. Buzz.
  • Toyota RAV4 2026: all-hybrid lineup from LE to GR Sport, plus the 320 hp plug-in hybrids.
  • Tesla: Cybertruck AWD and Cyberbeast, and the 2020 Model S and Model X (Long Range Plus and Performance with Ludicrous).
  • The Tesla Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, the 2019 RAV4 and the Lincoln Aviator, Corsair and Nautilus have new, more detailed bodies and interiors. The Lincolns are now 2026 models.
  • Each new car's drive-mode button has its real modes: Mazda Normal / Sport / Off-Road / Towing, VW Eco / Comfort / Sport / Individual plus Snow and Offroad on 4MOTION, RAV4 Eco / Normal / Sport / Trail / Snow, Cybertruck Chill / Standard / Sport (Beast) / Overland / Baja. Hybrids and plug-ins get an EV button.
  • Fixed: seat headrest posts in the new interiors sat in front of the driver's face.

Mazda screens

  • New CX-5: the 15.6-inch Google built-in touchscreen (Google Maps, your CX-5, the audio card, and the bottom bar with climate, home, maps, music, apps, settings, volume and SYNC) and the new digital cluster with its angled frames and the lane view in the middle.
  • Other Mazdas: the black Mazda Connect screen with Information, Entertainment, Communication, Navigation and Settings, the clock, and Apple CarPlay / Android Auto. Every entry opens its page. They also get the three-dial cluster: tachometer, centre speedometer with Drive Information, and temperature and fuel.

City traffic

  • Buses, ambulances, fire engines, garbage trucks, police SUVs, street sweepers, tow trucks and utility trucks now drive around as traffic. You can't pick them. Traffic and your driver assists leave the right gap behind the long ones, and they're heavy if you hit them.

Version 105 · U turns off front and rear auto braking

  • The U key now switches automatic emergency braking off (or back on) for both the front and the rear at once. With it off, the forward collision warning and the parking sensors still beep, but the car won't brake for you.

Version 104 · Cadillac CT4 and CT5 removed

  • The Cadillac CT4, CT4-V, CT4-V Blackwing, CT5, CT5-V and CT5-V Blackwing are no longer for sale. The LYRIQ, LYRIQ-V, OPTIQ, OPTIQ-V, VISTIQ and CELESTIQ are still here.

Version 103 · Mouse steering, VR, rear seat reminder

Driving

  • Batteries now run all the way down. The charge readout used to stop at 12%. Electric cars now drain to 0% and then stop with a "Battery empty" warning. Hybrids show their usable charge from 0 to 100%.
  • Mazda-style forward collision warning. When a crash is close, a big red BRAKE! warning fills the gauge cluster and the warning beeps get faster.
  • Rear Seat Reminder. If you drove for more than 20 seconds, switching the car off plays four chimes and shows "Look in rear seat" on the cluster. You can turn it off in Car → Controls.

Controls

  • Mouse steering (PC). Turn it on in Car → Controls. Move the mouse left or right of the screen's centre to steer. Hold the left button for gas and the right button for brake.
  • Phone in the car. Press the ` key (left of 1) to bring up your phone while driving.
  • VR on Meta Quest 3. Open the game in the Quest browser and tap VR, or use Car → Controls → Enter VR. You sit in the driver's seat with head tracking. Right trigger is gas, left trigger is brake, the left stick steers, A switches between Drive and Reverse, B changes the view and X sounds the horn.

Cars and character

  • The drive-mode button on the new Hyundai, BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Cadillac models now lists every real mode by name, for example Snow, Mud and Sand on the Tucson XRT, Sport Plus on BMW M models, and Trail, Rock and Sand on the G-Class.
  • Pick a man or a woman as your character in Car → Your character. They are used when you walk around and in the driver's seat.
  • On phones, the Screen button moved to the top left so it no longer covers other buttons.

Version 102 · Real Cadillac, BMW and Mercedes screens, calmer Mad Max

FSD

  • Mad Max no longer tailgates. It keeps about the same gap as Hurry and accelerates a little less hard, but still drives faster and changes lanes sooner.
  • Solid lines: the lane lines turn solid for the last 30 m before every junction, like real roads, and FSD never changes lanes there.
  • Use your blinker to change lanes: with FSD driving, signal left or right and it moves over as soon as there's a gap. In the solid-line zone it tells you it will stay in lane. If no gap shows up within 10 seconds, it cancels.

Cadillac

  • New cluster modelled on the real 33-inch display. A big speedometer fills blue up to the needle, with a straight tachometer bar, the Super Cruise view with "Auto Lane Change / Changing Lanes", range and fuel readouts, PRND and a radio card. A green bar lights along the top when Super Cruise is driving.
  • New home screen: the Google built-in grid (Audio, Phone, Maps, Google Assistant, Play Store, Climate, Auto Park Assist, myCadillac, Ambient Lighting, Wi-Fi Hotspot) over the blue wave, with the blue dock.
  • The CT4, CT5, LYRIQ, OPTIQ, VISTIQ and CELESTIQ now have the cluster behind the steering wheel and the touchscreen to its right on the same curved panel. Before, the CT5 showed one screen in the middle.
  • Removed the floating posts in front of the driver in every Cadillac.

BMW and Mercedes-Benz

  • BMW Curved Display: angular speed and rpm scales either side with a glowing fill, a big speed readout in the middle, and the blue / dark blue / red M stripe. The home screen has iDrive widget cards (Assistant, Values since Individual, Weather, Route Preview) and the climate bar.
  • Mercedes-Benz MBUX: two blue-lit round dials with red needles and trip info between them. The home screen has big Media, Comfort and Info tiles on the blue MBUX background.

Version 101 · Brand gauge clusters, digital and analog

New gauge clusters

  • Nissan, INFINITI, Subaru, Audi, Kia, Chrysler / Jeep / Ram / Dodge, Chevrolet / Buick / GMC, Cadillac and Acura now have their own cluster, each in a digital and an analog version.
  • Digital: each brand's look. Nissan has segmented red rings with ProPILOT in the middle. INFINITI has thin lavender rings. Subaru has blue arcs with the EyeSight cameras. Audi's virtual cockpit has red-tipped needles round a centre map. Kia's rings glow and change colour with the drive mode. Chrysler / Jeep / Ram / Dodge get blue arcs, GM segmented blue rings, and Cadillac thin champagne rings with Super Cruise. Acura has red-ringed dials.
  • Analog: real dials with needles, a redline on the tachometer and a small screen between them showing the clock, speed, gear, range and drive mode. Each brand has its own ring and needle colours, like Subaru's blue-lit faces and Cadillac's gold.
  • Every cluster shows your speed, gear, drive mode, fuel or battery range, the speed limit, cruise and lane-keeping status, turn signals and navigation.
  • New setting in Settings › Car: Gauge cluster, with Auto, Digital or Analog. Auto gives base trims that really have dials (S, SV, LX, WT, Subaru Base / Premium / Sport, Wrangler Sport and more) the analog cluster, and every other trim the digital one.

Screens

  • Subaru gets a STARLINK-style screen, INFINITI an InTouch-style screen and Acura its own red Google built-in style.

Version 99 · Finance step and a start-point picker

Builder

  • New last step in the builder: Finance. It shows your build's price, your checking balance, credit score and loan APR, then the ways to pay (test drive, your free first car, cash, finance or lease). For a loan it also shows the total you'll pay and the interest; for a lease it shows what buying the car out after 36 months would cost. Paying is no longer mixed in with the Accessories step.

Where do you want to go?

  • When you finish the builder, a pop-up lets you pick where to start: Downtown, the freeway, the parking garage, the proving ground, the hill, the river bridge and the rest. If you came from a drive, Where I was puts you back where you left off.

Version 98 · Faster garage, screens lined up

Parking garage frame rate

  • The garage model now draws about a third of the triangles it did. Back faces are skipped, the model is cut into tiles that are only drawn when in view, and the fine detail (rails, wheel stops, paint, sign text) only draws nearby and on your own level. From outside it draws about a fifth of the model.

Screens in the new cars

  • Cadillac's one long pillar-to-pillar display now shows the gauge cluster on the driver's side and the touchscreen on the right, instead of one picture across both. The CT4, CT5 and CELESTIQ driver's eye height is lowered so you no longer look at the roof lining.
  • Hyundai cars use the Hyundai gauge cluster and now a Hyundai Bluelink-style screen. BMW gets an iDrive-style screen and Mercedes-Benz an MBUX-style screen.

Hyundai (13)

  • Venue, Kona, Kona Electric, Tucson, Tucson Hybrid, Tucson Plug-in Hybrid, Santa Fe, Santa Fe Hybrid, Palisade, Palisade Hybrid, Santa Cruz pickup, IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9. They use the Hyundai gauge cluster and the Hyundai/Kia chime.

BMW (8)

Mercedes-Benz (16)
